rows.statement: There is no algorithm that, given an arbitrary sentence of first-order logic with at least one binary relation symbol, decides whether it is valid in every model.
If ZFC is consistent, then ZFC neither proves nor refutes the statement that every infinite set of real numbers is in bijection either with the natural numbers or with the reals.
There is no derivation of (p or not p), for a propositional variable p, in intuitionistic propositional natural deduction.
For every integer n greater than 2, there are no positive integers a, b, c with a^n + b^n = c^n.

Let F be the IEEE-754 binary16 interchange format, SMT-LIB `(_ FloatingPoint 5 11)`, and let RNE denote roundNearestTiesToEven. For all values a, b, c of F: if fp.leq(a, b) holds and neither fp.add(RNE, a, c) nor fp.add(RNE, b, c) is NaN, then fp.leq(fp.add(RNE, a, c), fp.add(RNE, b, c)). This is the binary16 instance of F:fp8-add-monotone-rne, and it is recorded `open` because AXEYUM HAS NOT SETTLED IT -- not because it is doubted.
Every consistent, effectively axiomatised formal system that interprets enough elementary arithmetic contains an arithmetical sentence that the system neither proves nor refutes.
